name: Helianthus

priority: mid-stem leaf width, outline and petiole
mid-stem venation: three conspicuous basal veins versus one strong midvein
head arrangement plus phyllary shape for flowering confirmation
study_strategy.warning: Do not use a dark disk, total height, number of heads, or opposite-vs-alternate leaves by itself. Both taxa are variable and may be cut or regrow. Start with a representative mid-stem leaf and attachment; confirm with the underside of a mature head.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Confirm a true sunflower head: many disk florets on one receptacle, yellow ray florets around the margin, and an involucre of green phyllaries beneath. Then use whole-plant architecture and leaves before tightening to phyllaries.
shared_traits: yellow ray florets surrounding many disk florets
involucre of phyllaries beneath each head
flattened cypselae that may carry short awns
shared_genus_recognition.caution: A yellow radiate Asteraceae head is not enough for Helianthus. Confirm the capitulum/involucre, then use leaves, branching pattern and phyllaries.

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Broad ovate to triangular/heart-based, often almost as wide as long; usually flat, stiff-hairy.
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Long narrow lanceolate; often folded upward along the single midvein (conduplicate) and arched downward.

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Usually 3 conspicuous veins rising from or near leaf base (triplinerved).
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Predominantly 1 conspicuous central vein (1-nerved); leaf often V-shaped in cross-section.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: VERY HIGH when representative mid-stem leaves are available

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Petiole obvious, often several cm; margin normally coarsely serrate.
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Sessile or short-petioled (typically 0–2 cm); margin usually entire, sometimes minutely serrulate.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: HIGH supporting; examine more than one leaf

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Annual from a taproot; does not persist as an established rhizomatous clone.
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Rhizomatous perennial; often returns in a multi-stem colony from one established patch.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: HIGH if root/crown or repeated-season evidence available

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Coarse, usually rough-hispid; often freely branching, but may have just one main terminal head.
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Rough to hairy, often erect and comparatively less freely branched; numerous leaves up the stem.

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Usually 1–9 heads, often at ends of branches; large-headed cultivated forms especially variable.
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Usually 3–15 heads, commonly spaced along upper stem in raceme- or spike-like display.

species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus annuus: Broader ovate to lance-ovate, commonly 5–8 mm wide, tips narrowing rather abruptly; hairy margins.
species_comparison_matrix.Helianthus maximiliani: Narrow lanceolate, about 2–3 mm wide, gradually narrowing to long slender pointed tips; hairy margins.

species_key.if: broad ovate/deltoid rough leaves on a usually branching annual
many narrow linear-lanceolate leaves, commonly conduplicate/folded and curving downward on an upright perennial

overlap_and_cautions: Both can be tall and carry yellow-rayed heads with dark centers; disk color is not diagnostic.
Both can have alternate leaves, and both may show opposite leaves near the base: leaf arrangement alone will mislead.
Growth form varies with mowing, disturbance, horticulture and age; annual sunflowers can be little-branched, Maximilian may branch.
Maximilian margins can be minutely toothed, and annual leaf shape varies; diagnose from a suite of representative mid-stem leaves.
The learning photos are not matched to the same scale or angle; use veins, folding and attachment, not their apparent relative size.
Helianthus identification may be confounded by hybridization and other perennial sunflowers; uncertain specimens stay Helianthus sp.

local_lookalike_routing.separate: First prove Helianthus-like head structure and involucre; then compare leaf arrangement, receptacle/phyllaries and fruit rather than flower color.
Do not route from height or yellow heads. Use leaf architecture/attachment and head underside; if those structures are missing, stop at the broader composite comparison.

visual_comparison.title: Annual vs Maximilian: leaves, nodes, and phyllaries
visual_comparison.subtitle: Six exact-species image anchors: first separate mature leaf form, then the leaf-to-stem attachment, then turn a mature head sideways. Images vary in camera scale; compare structure, not apparent pixel size.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Annual = broad, petioled, usually toothed, three strong basal veins. Maximilian = narrow, nearly stalkless, usually V-folded, one dominant midvein.

anatomy_lessons.title: 1 · Trace a mid-stem leaf to its node
anatomy_lessons.plain: A petiole is the stalk between the stem and leaf blade. Inspect several mature leaves halfway up the plant, not only basal or juvenile leaves.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: H. annuus usually has a broad toothed blade and obvious petiole; H. maximiliani often has a narrow blade attached nearly directly to the stem.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Attachment and blade outline remain usable before the plant flowers.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired mid-stem nodes, matched ruler and side view
anatomy_lessons.reference_status: existing source-linked node references available, not same-scale verified

anatomy_lessons.title: 2 · Count the strong veins and find the fold
anatomy_lessons.plain: Triplinerved means three prominent veins start near the blade base; conduplicate means folded lengthwise into a V.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Trace the basal veins of H. annuus and compare the dominant single midrib and often V-folded narrow H. maximiliani leaf.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Venation and longitudinal folding are stronger than color or head count.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: paired leaf front and cross-section macro, veins marked only after pixel review
anatomy_lessons.reference_status: existing linked leaf images are study references; vein-arrow placement unverified

anatomy_lessons.title: 3 · Turn a mature head sideways
anatomy_lessons.plain: The involucre is the set of green bracts beneath a sunflower head; each bract is a phyllary.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: H. annuus phyllaries often broad, about 5–8 mm wide; H. maximiliani often narrow, about 2–3 mm wide with long slender tips.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: Measured bract width is a useful flowering confirmation when stems have been cut or regrown.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: same-angle underside of mature heads with mm scale
anatomy_lessons.reference_status: two external licensed phyllary views already in visual_comparison, not locally installed

anatomy_lessons.title: 4 · Check the base and head sequence
anatomy_lessons.plain: An annual sunflower grows from a single-season root system; a perennial rhizome can send up shoots from connected underground stems.
anatomy_lessons.look_for: Compare annual taproot with rhizomatous H. maximiliani colony and document whether heads are terminal on branches or arranged along the upper stem.
anatomy_lessons.why_it_matters: The root system supports identification when foliage is atypical; head counts alone overlap.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: root/crown excavation and whole upper flowering stem, same-scale
anatomy_lessons.reference_status: no verified exact root-system photo assigned

comparison_cards.title: Annual versus Maximilian — leaf and node
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Choose three mature mid-stem leaves: broad petiolate 3-veined blades versus narrow short-stalked 1-nerved, often folded blades.
comparison_cards.measurable_tie_breaker: Petiole often several cm in annuus versus typically 0–2 cm in maximiliani; compare on the same plant stage.
comparison_cards.caution: Young shoots, drought, regrowth and unusual leaves can obscure any one character.

comparison_cards.title: Annual versus Maximilian — phyllaries
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Flip mature heads and measure a representative middle phyllary, not a tip alone.
comparison_cards.measurable_tie_breaker: Annuus often 5–8 mm wide with relatively abrupt taper; maximiliani often 2–3 mm wide with slender gradually tapering tips.
photo_requirements: underside of both mature heads at common scale
macro of a measured individual phyllary
comparison_cards.caution: Phyllaries vary within a head; compare several on intact, mature involucres.
